rationale: Algebraically the signal is just 1/(1+external issuance / intangible spend), i.e. a monotone rescaling of the gen-0 Knowledge_Capital_Per_External_Dollar idea whose cross-sectional variation is dominated by the well-documented composite issuance anomaly, and with COALESCE(xrd,0) every non-R&D firm collapses to exactly 0, creating a large degenerate mass that will drive the short leg as an "R&D-reporter" dummy rather than a self-funding measure.

The first leg is literally identical to the archive's Debt_Paydown_By_Intangible_Innovators (MA(xrd/sale,3) industry rank) and the second leg is the same net-payout-versus-issuance construct already tested in Payout_Funded_RD_Expansion, so replacing a rank with SIGN is a cosmetic robustness variant of two already-evaluated signals rather than a new mechanism.

Since gross profit is an order of magnitude larger than R&D for most firms, the "burn" leg is essentially negated gross profitability, so the product is largely the known gross-profitability × composite-issuance pair, and there is an internal inconsistency in that the expression's most extreme long leg (highly profitable firms issuing heavily) is described in the hypothesis only as "ordinary growth funding," not as an expected outperformer.

A within-firm time-series-position differencing of innovation intensity against issuance is genuinely distinct from the archive's cross-sectional rank products and from level-based issuance/R&D anomalies, is bounded and monotone with economically interpretable extremes, though the authors should check that COALESCE(xrd,0) constant-zero histories do not make the first TS_RANK degenerate for the many non-R&D firms.

Post-goodwill-impairment drift is an established published anomaly, and because gdwl is a component of intan the signal asserts that *falling* intangibles plus issuance predicts low returns while the archive's Externally_Financed_Intangible_Buildup asserts the opposite sign for *rising* intangibles plus issuance, a tension the proposal labels rather than resolves.

Advertising intensity is a legitimately unexplored conditioning variable here, but the second leg is the standard share-count-growth issuance anomaly and the claim of orthogonality to advertising level is wrong (the rank multiplier deliberately amplifies high-ad firms), while COALESCE(xad,0) leaves most firms tied at zero so the effective test rests on a thin advertiser subsample.
